note: Areas are approximate boxes (west, south, east, north). Tighten them after looking at real scenes.

hotspots.name: Caracas and La Guaira coast

rule.meaning: 12-day GUNW pairs spanning the Jun 24 earthquakes

hotspots.why: The M7.2 and M7.5 earthquakes of June 24, 2026 moved the ground by up to 60 cm, and NISAR mapped the shift.
hotspots.sensitive: Thousands of people died in these earthquakes. This story stays factual and respectful.

hotspots.name: Mexico City
hotspots.why: Decades of groundwater pumping make it one of the fastest-sinking cities on Earth.

hotspots.name: Jakarta
hotspots.why: A sinking coastal megacity; its subsidence is one reason Indonesia is building a new capital.

hotspots.name: Tehran plain
hotspots.why: Aquifer depletion is lowering the ground under a city of millions.

hotspots.name: San Joaquin Valley
hotspots.why: Farm pumping sinks the valley, with a seasonal rebound; dense GNSS stations make it ideal for checking results.

hotspots.name: Joshimath and the Uttarakhand Himalaya
hotspots.why: A hill town that cracked and sank in 2023, on slopes that creep across the region.

hotspots.name: Reykjanes Peninsula
hotspots.why: Repeated magma intrusions and eruptions since 2023 lift and drop the ground near Grindavik.
hotspots.caution: High latitude: L-band ionosphere effects need extra care here.

hotspots.name: Campi Flegrei
hotspots.why: A restless caldera is lifting the ground under a suburb of Naples.

hotspots.name: Tonle Sap
hotspots.why: Each monsoon the lake swells several times over and its river flows backwards: a textbook seasonal dance.

hotspots.name: Pantanal
hotspots.why: The largest tropical wetland on Earth; recent droughts and fires show its rhythm breaking.

hotspots.name: Brahmaputra valley
hotspots.why: Monsoon floods spread under thick cloud, where only radar can see the water.

hotspots.name: Sudd wetland
hotspots.why: A vast wetland whose floods have displaced communities in recent years.

hotspots.name: Amazon arc of deforestation
hotspots.why: Forest is cleared and burned under near-constant cloud, but L-band radar still sees the canopy.

hotspots.name: Canadian boreal forest
hotspots.why: Record-breaking recent fire seasons leave burn scars that radar maps through smoke.

hotspots.name: Punjab and Haryana
hotspots.why: A rice and wheat rotation whose harvest timing is linked to crop-residue burning.

hotspots.name: Mekong Delta
hotspots.why: Up to three rice crops a year, each one starting with flooded paddies.

hotspots.name: South African maize belt
hotspots.why: NASA used NISAR to show a South African growing season; this box is a best guess at the region, so check it.

hotspots.name: Shisper Glacier
hotspots.why: A surging glacier that has dammed a lake and set off outburst floods in the Hunza valley.

hotspots.name: Sermeq Kujalleq (Jakobshavn)
hotspots.why: One of the fastest-flowing glaciers on Earth.
hotspots.caution: High latitude: L-band ionosphere effects need extra care here.
